statement.p: Calculate the following integral: \int x^{3} \ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) \, dx
and then use the integration-by-parts formula to find that
and finally, we finish evaluating to get that \displaystyle \int x^{3} \ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) \, dx =

hint.p: We pick u and dv so that dv can be integrated, and then (ideally) u gets simpler.
We do not know how to easily integrate \ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right), so that must be u.
Then everything else in the integral must equal dv. So dv =x^{3}dx.
Since u=\ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) we take the derivative to get that du= \frac{1}{x}dx =\frac{1}{x} \, dx.
Since dv =x^{3}dx we integrate to get that v= \frac{1}{4} x^{4}

Next, remember that the integration by parts formula says that \int u \, dv = u\cdot v - \int v \, du So, substituting in what we already know are u, \ v,\ du and dv, we get that \int x^{3} \ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) \, dx = \ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) \cdot \frac{1}{4} x^{4} - \int \frac{1}{4} x^{4} \cdot \frac{1}{x} \, dx Now cancel the x's in that last integral, and it's a basic integral (power rule) so you can evaluate it.

solution.p: The integration by parts formula says that \int u \, dv = u\cdot v - \int v \, du So, substituting in, we get that \int x^3 \ln(9 x) \, dx = \ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) \cdot \frac{1}{4}x^{4} - \int \frac{1}{4}x^{4} \cdot \frac{1}{x} \, dx =\ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) \cdot \frac{1}{4}x^{4} - \int \frac{1}{4}x^{3} \, dx Lastly, we integrate the second part, so the answer is \int x^3 \ln(9 x) \, dx = \frac{1}{4}x^{4} \cdot \ln\mathopen{}\left(9x\right) - \frac{1}{16}x^{4}+C
